lines.text: This hot dog has cost $1.50 since 1985.
lines.spoken: This hot dog has cost a dollar fifty since 1985.

lines.text: Adjusted for inflation, it would cost over $4.50 today.
lines.spoken: Adjusted for inflation, it would cost over four fifty today.

lines.text: And Costco's CEO says the price will not change as long as he's around.
Why? Because Costco runs on razor-thin margins.
Of every dollar it takes in, it keeps about three cents as profit.
In its last fiscal year, members paid $5.9 billion just for the right to shop there.
lines.spoken: In its last fiscal year, members paid five point nine billion dollars just for the right to shop there.

lines.text: That's equal to nearly two-thirds of Costco's entire profit.
So the hot dog isn't really a menu item. It's a signal: everything in this building is a deal.
Keep that promise, and people keep paying just to walk in.
